title: MLOps (Machine Learning Operations)
body: The practice of applying DevOps principles to machine learning pipelines. Encompasses experiment tracking, model versioning, automated testing, deployment, monitoring, and retraining. Aims to operationalize ML models reliably and at scale.

title: MLflow
body: An open-source platform for managing machine learning workflows. Provides experiment tracking (MLflow Tracking), model registry, model serving, and project reproducibility. Integrates with Databricks for unified ML operations.

title: MLflow Experiment Tracking
body: MLflow's system for logging parameters, metrics, and artifacts during model training runs. Enables data scientists to compare experiments, track hyperparameter tuning, and reproduce results.

title: MLflow Model Registry
body: A centralized repository for model versioning, staging (Staging/Production), and lineage tracking. Enables teams to approve models, track transitions between stages, and maintain audit trails of model deployments.

title: Model Staging (Development, Staging, Production)
body: MLOps practice of promoting models through environments before production. Development: active experimentation; Staging: pre-production testing; Production: live serving. MLflow Model Registry manages these transitions.

title: Databricks Model Serving
body: Fully managed REST API serving for ML models on Databricks. Handles autoscaling, A/B testing, model shadowing, and canary deployments. Integrates with MLflow Model Registry for seamless deployment.

title: Mosaic AI (Databricks)
body: Databricks' managed platform for end-to-end ML workflows. Combines data preparation, model training, experiment tracking, model serving, and LLM operations. Provides Mosaic AI Agent Framework for GenAI applications.

title: Feature Store
body: A centralized repository for machine learning features (transformations of raw data). Enables reuse of features across models, ensures consistency between training and serving, and manages feature versioning and lineage.

title: Databricks Feature Store
body: Native feature store on Databricks supporting both batch and real-time feature serving. Tracks feature lineage, enables point-in-time joins for training, and serves features via online store for real-time predictions.

title: Tecton Feature Store
body: Independent feature store platform that unifies batch and real-time feature computation. Enables teams to define features once and use across training and serving, with built-in monitoring and lineage tracking.

title: Model Monitoring / Model Observability
body: Continuous tracking of model performance in production (accuracy drift, data drift, concept drift, bias). Enables early detection of model degradation and triggers automated retraining or alerts to data science teams.

title: Data Drift
body: Change in the statistical properties of input data over time, causing model performance degradation. Example: if claims fraud patterns change seasonally but the model wasn't trained on recent data, it suffers data drift.

title: Concept Drift
body: Change in the relationship between input features and target variable over time, even if feature distributions remain constant. Example: insurance pricing rules change, but historical claims patterns no longer predict risk accurately.

title: Model Retraining
body: Process of re-running model training on fresh data to recover from drift or improve performance. Can be scheduled (daily, weekly) or triggered by monitoring alerts (drift detected, accuracy below threshold).

title: Model Explainability / Interpretability
body: Techniques for understanding why a trained model makes specific predictions. Critical in insurance for regulatory compliance and user trust. Examples: SHAP values, LIME, feature importance scores.

title: SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations)
body: A game-theoretic approach to explain model predictions. Computes each feature's contribution to a prediction based on Shapley values. Provides global and local explanations; widely used in regulated industries.

title: LIME (Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations)
body: A technique for explaining individual predictions by fitting a simple, interpretable model locally around the data point. Model-agnostic (works with any model). Provides local explanations that are easier to understand than global SHAP.

metadata.attribution: Marco Ribeiro, Sameer Singh, Carlos Guestrin

title: Feature Importance
body: Measure of how much each input feature contributes to model predictions. Calculated differently across model types (tree-based: Gini importance, SHAP, permutation importance). Helps identify key drivers of predictions.

title: Model Bias / Fairness
body: Systematic errors where model predictions favor certain groups over others. Example: insurance model underestimating risk for specific demographics. MLOps requires detecting and mitigating bias.

title: Batch Scoring / Batch Inference
body: Process of generating predictions for a large dataset in one go (as opposed to real-time). Databricks Jobs run batch scoring pipelines to score millions of records overnight, updating analytics tables.

title: Real-Time Scoring / Online Inference
body: Generating predictions on-demand through an API for individual requests. Requires low-latency serving infrastructure. Databricks Model Serving and feature stores support real-time scoring.

title: A/B Testing (in ML)
body: Comparing two model versions (A and B) in production by routing traffic to each. Enables safe rollout of new models and quantifies performance gains. Databricks Model Serving natively supports A/B testing.

title: Canary Deployment
body: Gradually rolling out a new model to production by serving it to a small percentage of traffic initially, then increasing percentage if metrics look good. Reduces risk of bad models impacting all users.

title: Model Shadowing
body: Running a new model in parallel to the production model without using its predictions for real decisions. Allows observation of model behavior and performance metrics before full rollout.

title: Model Artifacts
body: Files generated during model training and needed for inference: trained model weights, preprocessing transformations, vocabulary files, configuration files. MLflow tracks and versions artifacts.

title: Model Serialization (Pickle, Parquet, ONNX)
body: Process of converting trained models to storable formats for deployment. MLflow supports multiple formats (sklearn pickle, TensorFlow SavedModel, ONNX). ONNX enables cross-platform model portability.

title: SageMaker Pipelines (AWS)
body: AWS service for orchestrating end-to-end ML workflows. Handles data preparation, training, hyperparameter tuning, evaluation, and deployment steps. Integrates with SageMaker training and model registry.

title: CI/CD for Machine Learning
body: Applying continuous integration and deployment practices to ML. Includes automated testing of data quality, model performance, and staged deployments. Ensures model changes are validated before production.
